group.passage:
Developed by Boston Dynamics in the USA, Spot is a compact, mobile four-legged robot capable of moving across almost any surface while sensing its surroundings. Despite its initial mission to inspect industrial sites, conduct hazardous missions, and make deliveries since becoming available for rental in 2019, Spot is now being modified to serve as a guide dog by a group at Queensland University of Technology. This cutting-edge project seeks to solve the significant obstacles faced by visually-impaired people, especially those concerning traditional guide dogs.
Research participants with vision problems shared their experiences with their furry companions. They described the difficulties they encountered. For instance, traveling internationally with a guide dog is possible but extremely challenging due to quarantine requirements and paperwork. Moreover, there are times when guide dogs become ill and thus unable to continue their service. Still, there are some people waiting on guide dog wait lists or living too far from an organization that provides assistance animals. And, some wish to have a guide dog, but they find it difficult to care for an animal.
Robotic guide dogs can overcome these difficulties. Unlike living dogs, which require extensive and continuous training, a robotic guide dog like Spot can have its programming updated as needed. This feature is particularly beneficial for guide dog users traveling internationally, as they could access reprogrammed robotic dogs at each destination, thereby avoiding the need for animal quarantine. On the other hand, the investment in training a living guide dog can also be reduced. According to Guide Dogs Queensland, it takes two years to breed guide dogs specifically for service and costs $50,000 per dog for training. Nevertheless, only about 40 percent of the puppies bred are qualified to graduate from their program.
[[4]] For many people, technology will never compare to the value of a well-trained dog. Companionship, intuition, and a dog’s ability to see ahead and then make early actions to guide someone safely is unbeatable.

questions.stem: What is the primary application of Spot, initially developed by Boston Dynamics?

options.A: To serve as a companion for families and individuals.
options.B: To undertake safety checks and risk-related tasks.
options.C: To function as a security guard for properties.
options.D: To perform as an entertainer at various shows.

questions.stem: What challenge is NOT faced by traditional guide dogs and their users in this passage?

options.A: The inconvenience caused by guide dogs’ health condition.
options.B: The restrictions and complications when traveling abroad.
options.C: The requirement for ongoing training and attentive care.
options.D: The lack of medical support and training organizations.

questions.stem: Which of the following comparisons between the two types of Guide Dogs is true?

options.A: Robotic guide dogs require the same amount of training cost as living guide dogs.
options.B: Robotic guide dogs can have their software updated to overcome living guide dogs’ limitations.
options.C: Robotic guide dogs are less capable of handling complex environments than living guide dogs.
options.D: Robotic guide dogs have been widely accepted and preferred over living guide dogs.

questions.stem: Which is the most suitable sentence to fill the ❶?

options.A: Spot’s advanced technology makes traditional guide dogs outdated, offering a more efficient solution.
options.B: This project primarily aims to improve Spot’s industrial capabilities, with a secondary objective as a guide dog.
options.C: The project’s goal is not to replace traditional guide dogs but to fill gaps in current assistance options.
options.D: Guide dog training programs are expected to change with the introduction of robotic guide dogs like Spot.
